headline: PM Tarique Rahman leaves for Tokyo on 4-day state visit
summary: The Prime Minister is leading a 15-member delegation to Japan at the invitation of PM Sanae Takaichi.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has departed from Dhaka for a four-day state visit to Japan, accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman.
The Prime Minister left Shahjalal International Airport around 12:15 am on Monday via a commercial flight operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
He is visiting Japan at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and is leading a high-level 15-member delegation.
The delegation includes Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance and Planning Advisor Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir.
Also accompanying the PM are State Minister for Power Aninda Islam Amit, Telecoms Advisor Rehan Asif Asad, and Bangladesh Bank Governor Mostaqur Rahman.
The group also includes BIDA Chairman Chowdhury Ashik Mahmud Bin Harun, Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam, and several senior government officials.
Political representatives from Hifazat e-Islam and the Nezam-e-Islam Party, as well as the Amjanatar Dal, are also part of the delegation.

headline_marked: Biman [[extends Riyadh and Dammam flight suspension]] till Nov 4
headline: Biman extends Riyadh and Dammam flight suspension till Nov 4
summary: The national carrier cited passenger safety amid continued attacks on Saudi airports for the extension.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has extended the suspension of all flights between Dhaka and Riyadh, as well as Dhaka and Dammam, until November 4.
The airline stated that the decision was made to ensure passenger safety following continued attacks on airports within Saudi Arabia.
Previously, Biman had suspended Dhaka-Dammam flights from October 23 to 25 and all Dhaka-Riyadh flights until October 31.
Despite these suspensions, Biman continues to operate two daily flights between Dhaka and Jeddah to meet passenger demand, a service that will remain active until November 4.
Passengers with urgent travel needs are advised to use Jeddah or Madinah airports for travel to Saudi Arabia or for returning to Bangladesh.
The airline has urged affected passengers to contact the nearest sales offices for ticketing and travel information. Further updates on flight schedules will be announced later.
caption:
